abstract: Highlights • Candidate biomarkers (i.e., brain-derived neurotrophic factor, β-hydroxybutyrate, cathepsin B, kynurenine, fibroblast growth factor 21, soluble vascular cell adhesion molecule-1) did not mediate the effects of exercise on brain health outcomes. • The macrophage scavenger receptor type-I (MSR1) is a membrane glycoprotein, never before related to exercise, that is expressed in macrophages and involved in pathological processes such as atherosclerosis, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, and neurological diseases. • Our discovery analysis, a panel of 92 neurology-related proteins, identified a reduction effect of exercise on blood-circulating MRS1. • Exercise-induced changes in MRS1 did not mediate changes in brain health outcomes.
